clue.text: Times has to cut education programme

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the phrase before it loses its final letter

blocks.note: eras are periods of time
'has to' means must

explanation.surface: Budget pressures mean an education scheme must be trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: ERAS plus MUS(t) gives ERASMUS, the European student-exchange scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus is the European Union scheme that funds students studying at universities in other countries.

clue.text: Seasick, regularly exercises to secure a welcome relief

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so take every other letter
to secure something is to hold it fast inside

blocks.note: second, fourth and sixth letters
PE is physical education, school exercises
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seasick passenger does exercises regularly, which brings welcome relief.
explanation.walkthrough: ESC and PE together hold A.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape is a welcome break from something unpleasant, a release or diversion that brings relief.

clue.text: Breaks wind, covering head to limit nasty smell, and performs emergency stop

indicators.note: covering the head hides it from view, so the first letter disappears
to limit is to hem in, so letters close around the next piece

blocks.note: to break wind is to fart
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: Someone with wind tries to stifle the smell, then hits the brakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering head' sounds like hiding a face from the smell, but it tells you to hide the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To abort is to halt a mission or process abruptly, as in an emergency stop.

clue.text: Daisy spread ceremonial procedure around university

indicators.note: the joined words are placed around the final piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: marge is short for margarine, a spread
a rite is a ceremonial act
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A daisy is spread over the ground at a university ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: Marge is the everyday British short form of margarine.
explanation.definitionFit: Marguerite is the name for the ox-eye daisy and similar white-petalled flowers with yellow centres.

clue.text: Host is primarily sympathetic and friendly

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so just the first letter is wanted

blocks.note: first letter only
warm means friendly and kind

explanation.surface: A good host is above all sympathetic and friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a party-giver but means a crowd, as in 'a host of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a large crowd or multitude of people or things, as in 'a host of angels'.

clue.text: Cunning to spread some chaos

indicators.note: one word is spread out so that it stretches around the other

blocks.note: 'some' as in 'have you any?'
arch means slyly knowing or cunning

explanation.surface: A sly plan to sow a little disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like part of the definition's picture of chaos, but it tells one word to stretch around another.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is a state of lawless disorder with no government, a complete breakdown of order.

clue.text: Attachment of plaster without protective equipment? Not British!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first piece goes around the second
the British letter is not wanted, so it is taken out

blocks.note: a sticking plaster is a small adhesive bandage
PPE is personal protective equipment
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Applying a plaster without protective gear, and doing it in a non-British way.
explanation.walkthrough: A plaster in Britain is an adhesive dressing for a small wound; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is something attached to a larger thing, such as a limb on a body.

clue.text: A fuel for ovens

blocks.note: taken as written
gas is a fuel

explanation.surface: Choosing a fuel to power ovens.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron range cooker, a fixture of British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Agas are a brand of large heat-storage range cookers, so they are ovens.

clue.text: King's personal energy enthralling French city

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one piece holds the other inside

blocks.note: chi is the life force or vital energy in Chinese thought
Arles is a city in Provence

explanation.surface: A monarch's personal charisma captivates a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles I was King of England, Scotland and Ireland, executed in 1649 after the Civil War.

clue.text: Obedient Tory at last skilfully handling ousting leader

indicators.note: at last points to the end, so only the closing letter is used
the leader is ousted, so the first letter is thrown out

blocks.note: last letter only
to wield a tool is to handle it skilfully

explanation.surface: A compliant Conservative deftly manages to depose the party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: WIELDING drops its W.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding describes someone who gives way readily to others, so compliant and submissive.

clue.text: Singing group folded sheets, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so go by the sound

blocks.note: a quire is a set of paper sheets folded together

explanation.surface: A singing group handles their folded song sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire is a paper-trade term for twenty-four or twenty-five sheets, and it is pronounced the same as the singing group.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised body of singers, typically performing in a church or concert.

clue.text: I like lap dancing, meat and beer?

definitions.text: I like lap dancing, meat and beer

indicators.note: letters that dance move about and change places

blocks.note: taken as written
ham is a meat
ale is a beer

explanation.surface: A macho boast of liking strip clubs, meat and beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the sort of thing a stereotypical alpha male might say, while 'lap dancing' also supplies ALP, then HAM and ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpha male is a dominant, macho man, the type caricatured as loving lap dancing, steak and beer.

clue.text: Cricketer dropping catch utilises Mitchell Marsh's tips batting second

indicators.note: the tips of these words are their front ends, so take just the opening letter of each

blocks.note: a cowpat is an animal dropping
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the opening letters of three words
a batsman who is batting is in
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An Australian cricketer drops a catch off Mitchell Marsh, another Australian player, batting at number two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping catch' reads as a fielding blunder, but it splits into PAT and C. Pat Cummins and Mitchell Marsh are both Australian Test cricketers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat Cummins is an Australian fast bowler who has captained his national Test side.

clue.text: Ran away from policeman arresting unqualified driver

indicators.note: to arrest is to seize and hold, so one piece holds the other inside

blocks.note: a fed is an American federal agent
L for learner, the plate on a learner's car

explanation.surface: Someone fled when a policeman tried to arrest a learner driver.
explanation.walkthrough: L sits inside FED. In Britain a learner driver must show an L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Fled is the past tense of flee, meaning escaped or bolted from danger.

clue.text: Both of us marching in part of Yorkshire

blocks.note: we is both of us
striding is walking purposefully, as when marching

explanation.surface: Two people march together across a Yorkshire district.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Riding was one of the three historic divisions of Yorkshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: The West Riding was a historic administrative division of the county of Yorkshire in northern England.

clue.text: Excuse to go round valleys for lecture

indicators.note: one word goes round the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: an excuse is a reason given
dales are valleys, especially in northern England

explanation.surface: Someone looks for an excuse to tour the valleys.
explanation.walkthrough: Dales is the usual word for valleys in northern England, as in the Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.definitionFit: To lecture someone is to scold them at length, which is what 'read someone a lesson' means as an idiom.

clue.text: Perhaps Nirvana are following fertile fans

indicators.note: to fan is to spread out, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: a is the abbreviation for are, a metric unit of area
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nirvana, the rock band, are pursued by enthusiastic fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Nirvana looks like the grunge band, but here it is the Buddhist state of release beyond this life.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism nirvana is a state after death and rebirth end, one example of an existence beyond earthly life.

clue.text: One may turn back at work?

definitions.text: One may turn back at work?

blocks.clueFragment: One may turn back at work?
blocks.note: surface reading: a worker who returns to the job after time away
setter's reading: a cricket delivery that spins, coming back in to the batter once it is in play

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an off break is a ball spun by the bowler so it turns in from the off side; read another way, someone off their break is back at work.
explanation.definitionFit: An off break is a spinning cricket delivery that turns after bouncing, deviating from off side towards leg.

clue.text: Ramshackle tram taking ages shifting Taylor Swift?

indicators.note: something ramshackle is falling apart, so its letters are rebuilt in a new order
letters that are shifting move around and change places
one piece takes in the other, holding it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rickety tram takes forever to move Taylor Swift around.
explanation.definitionFit: Taylor Swift is an example of a hugely famous performer, a superstar; the question mark marks her as one instance.

clue.text: Quick way to get property on board

blocks.note: fleet means swift
a street is a road or way

explanation.surface: Advice on a fast way to acquire property, or to get aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a Monopoly board: Fleet Street, the London street once home to the newspapers, is one of its squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet Street is one of the squares a player can buy in the London edition of the Monopoly board game.

clue.text: Save time following move

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the piece named first is placed second

blocks.note: to budge is to move slightly
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Saving time by following one's next move.
explanation.definitionFit: To budget is to economise and plan spending carefully, so as to save money.

clue.text: Superior gambler

blocks.note: first meaning: of a higher standard
second meaning: one who bets

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the word as 'one who bets', a rarer spelling sometimes written bettor.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the comparative of good, meaning of higher quality, and a noun for someone who places wagers.

clue.text: Head to lament leaving Missouri

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: to bemoan is to lament
MO is the US state abbreviation for Missouri

explanation.surface: A head of department mourning someone who has left Missouri.
explanation.walkthrough: Bean is old slang for the head, as in 'use your bean'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean is informal slang for a person's head or brain, used in phrases like 'a knock on the bean'.

clue.text: Sex worker is expert in avoiding law

indicators.note: the word before it is avoided, so it is left out of what follows

blocks.note: a pro is a professional or expert
taken as written; these letters are the ones removed
an institute is an established law or principle, as in legal institutes

explanation.surface: A sex worker is skilled at staying on the right side of the law.
explanation.walkthrough: INSTITUTE without IN leaves STITUTE. 'Institute' as a noun for a law or rule is a rarer sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A prostitute is a person who engages in sexual activity for payment, a sex worker.

clue.text: Terrace I put outside hotel

indicators.note: one piece is placed on the outside of the other, wrapping it

blocks.note: the self is the I, one's own person
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone puts a terrace outside a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace and a shelf can both be a flat ledge or level step cut into a slope or rock face.

clue.text: Ring Henry and Oscar

blocks.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Phoning two friends called Henry and Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call, but it is a circle of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a circle of light shown around a saint's head, a glowing ring.

clue.text: Taximeter running for a further period

indicators.note: something running is in motion, so the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cab's meter keeps ticking for longer than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra time is an additional period added to a sports match, such as football, when scores are level.

clue.text: Getting others to conceal lump

indicators.note: the words conceal the answer within their letters, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Persuading other people to hide a lump of something.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block or lump of cast metal, typically gold or silver bars.

clue.text: Knocked back liquor and wine, ultimately receiving fine for singing along to tune

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, but read as turned back the word runs right to left
ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter is used
one piece receives the other, taking it inside

blocks.note: arak is an anise-flavoured spirit from the Middle East
last letter only
OK means fine

explanation.surface: After downing spirits and wine, someone is fined for singing along to a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: KARA, then E receiving OK at its front to make OKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Karaoke is entertainment where people sing along with recorded backing tracks to popular tunes.

clue.text: Boxer, perhaps, and female rowing crew cycling next to river

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round, taking the first and putting it at the end

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
an eight is a racing boat with eight rowers
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A boxer and a women's rowing crew cycling along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: EIGHT with its first letter moved to the end becomes IGHTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is one example of a fighter, someone who fights in combat sports; 'perhaps' marks the example.
